# How to Punt in H2H 9-Cat

<sub>Proposed by the synthesis, not on the user's list.</sub>

**Summary.** In our 12-team 9-cat league, draft and bid for value first, and let a punt come out of the players you actually land. Turnovers are the safest punt. Steals, blocks, threes and FT% are fine to punt. Points and assists are bad punts. Never pay a player's punt-ranked price in the auction, and do not punt so heavily that your weekly volume collapses before the 2027-03-28 finish.

## What punting is and when to do it

Punting only applies to category leagues like ours. It means ignoring one or more categories and acting as if they do not exist. You are not trying to be bad in them. You stop caring, move your resources to the other categories, and accept whatever happens. You will still win the punted category some weeks. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=69), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=152), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=389), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2611), [09-07](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=791))

The logic is simple. Fantasy value is finite. If you spread it over eight categories instead of nine, you are stronger in each of the eight. A head-to-head week needs only 5 category wins out of 9, so even balanced teams end up giving up something in the playoffs. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=240), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=454))

Timing in our auction: do not open 2026-10-18 with a fixed punt plan. Early on, bid for value. Lean into a punt later if your first buys point to one. If a player goes well below his value, buy him and adjust the build afterwards. You can change your punt at any time: mid draft, mid season, or mid week on waivers and in trades before the 2027-03-04 deadline. ([08-11](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=1376), [09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1763), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=799))

The experts disagree on how much punting matters. One side says punting wins leagues and becomes more viable with more teams, more categories and deeper leagues. The other side says people overindex on it, and that you win with big value picks and smart waiver moves. They also differ on Giannis. One note says that if you draft a bad FT shooter like Giannis, you should punt FT%. Another says taking Giannis does not mean you have to punt free throws. Both sides agree on one practical rule: the punt follows value. It does not drive your bids. ([09-16](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=2381), [08-11](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=1376), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=489), [09-17](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=323), [10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=856))

## Which categories to punt

Turnovers are the easiest punt. Lloyd ignores turnovers in every head-to-head league, and his DURANT ranking for H2H leaves them out. Anyone buying high-usage, high-value players cannot avoid turnovers anyway. Working hard to keep turnovers low hurts the rest of the team. Use turnovers only as a tiebreaker between two otherwise identical players. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=549), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1857), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=2271), [09-17](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=303), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1765), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=2232))

High-variance categories are good punts: steals, blocks, threes and FT%. You will still steal some of them by surprise in a given week. Stable high-volume categories like points and assists are bad punts, because when you are weak there you lose them almost every week. Low-scoring players are harder to build around unless you are comfortable punting points. ([07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2722), [08-11](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=506))

Do not decide on an FT% punt because of one bad season. Free throw percentage swings a lot in both directions. When checking a player before the auction, do not let a single poor FT year push you into a punt build. ([08-09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1274))

If a category is already too weak to recover, do not buy a one-category specialist to fix it. Also do not overindex on chasing a weak category like assists. Early two-category players leave holes you then have to fill. ([09-15](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1166), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=864), [09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=960))

## Watch the correlations

Categories move together. High assists go with high turnovers. Low turnovers go with low points and low assists. High blocks go with high rebounds and high FG%. A punt in one category therefore drags others along if you chase the wrong player type. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=588))

Punting blocks: do not chase low-block players, or your rebounds and FG% fall too. Punting assists: turnovers come down on their own, but check your threes, steals and FT%, because low-assist players often struggle there. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=620), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=630))

Punting FT%: free throws are linked to points, threes and assists. If you buy only bad FT shooters, you are really punting four categories. With a Giannis-type anchor, keep every player on your target list and buy guard stats early: assists, threes, steals. The rule from the notes is to draft guards in two of the next three rounds. In our auction, that means two of your next three significant buys should be guards. You do not need to chase low-FT players. ([09-07](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=568), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=524), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=756), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=561), [09-17](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=323))

Keep positional cover while punting. Our lineup has G, G, G, F, F, F, C and three Util slots, with daily changes. Have at least two to three eligible players at each position, or you give up games during the week. ([09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=662))

## Why punt rankings mislead and why not to overpay

Punt rankings lie. They remove your weak category but not everyone else's, so they overstate how much a player helps you. Lloyd's DURANT ranking tries to correct for this. Overall 9-cat ranks can mislead in the other direction. If you punt FT, a drop in a player's FT% barely matters to you, even when his overall rank falls a lot. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=709), [07-16](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=2097))

In the auction, do not flip a punt toggle and pay the inflated punt value. Overpaying for a player because he fits your build is not value. Do not push up the bids on players who gain value in punt rankings, such as bad FT% shooters, just to secure them. Set your price limit from his standard value. Buy him only if he comes in at or below it. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=913), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2379))

The reason is practical. Other managers are usually not bidding on him for your punt, so the fit is a discount you collect, not a premium you pay. Every dollar you overspend from the 200 USD budget is a dollar missing from the value buys that win leagues. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=913), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=489))

## Heavy punting adds variance

Heavy punting means low volume and more weekly variance. Depending on the format, that can cost you a playoff spot. If the top six of 12 make the playoffs, you can punt more heavily. If only the top four make it, punting four categories may keep you out. ([09-07](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=1394), [09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=281))

For our league: our playoffs run weeks 19, 20 and 21 and end on 2027-03-28. Check in the league settings how many teams qualify before choosing a multi-category punt. Default to one punt, usually turnovers, plus at most one more from the high-variance group. That gives you enough categories to reach 5 wins most weeks. ([09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=281), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=454), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2722))

Punting is more viable in deeper leagues with more teams. Ours drafts 144 players and leaves the rest on waivers. With up to 6 adds per week, use FAB and trades to steer the build in season, not to rescue a category that is already lost. ([09-16](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=2381), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=799), [09-15](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1166))
